words.n: The (masculine); la (feminine); l' before a vowel or mute h; les (plural). As an object pronoun: him, her, it, them, before the verb.
Of, from. Joins with le and les: du, des. Also the partitive, some (du pain, de l'eau), which becomes de after a negative (pas de pain).

To be. Also the helper verb for the passé composé of verbs of movement and change (aller, venir, partir, naître, mourir ...) and of every reflexive verb; the past participle then agrees with the subject.
To have. The helper verb for most passé composé forms. Also for age (j'ai trente ans), and for hunger, thirst, heat, cold, fear (avoir faim, avoir peur).
To, at, in (a town). Joins with le and les: au, aux. Also for what something is for or has (une tasse à café, la fille aux yeux bleus).
That (je pense que ...); than (plus grand que); what (Que veux-tu?). Shortens to qu' before a vowel. Ne ... que means only.
This, that (ce livre); cet before a vowel, cette (feminine), ces (plural). C'est: it is, this is.
Who (Qui est là?); also that, which, when it is the subject in the clause that follows.
In (a country, a month, a language: en France, en mai); by (en train). As a pronoun: some, of it, of them; from there.
To do, to make. Also the weather (il fait beau), and faire + infinitive: to have something done (faire réparer).
Oneself, himself, herself, themselves: makes a verb reflexive (se lever, to get up) or reciprocal (ils s'aiment, they love each other). Me, te, se, nous, vous, se by person.
ex: Je me lève à sept heures.

words.n: One, people; in speech mostly we. Takes the il form of the verb.
Half of most negatives: ne ... pas (not), ne ... jamais (never), ne ... rien (nothing), ne ... personne (nobody), ne ... plus (no longer). In speech the ne often drops.
ex: Il ne mange jamais de viande.

words.n: Can, to be able; may (Puis-je ...? in formal questions).
You (one person you know well); vous for several people or politely to one.
There (to a place already named); also stands for à + a thing.
To go. Aller + infinitive is the everyday near future.

words.g: must; to have to; to owe
words.n: Must, to have to; to owe. In the conditionnel, should (tu devrais).
To want. Je voudrais (conditionnel) is the polite I'd like.

words.g: to know (a fact); to know how to
words.n: To know (a fact, how to). Connaître is to know a person or a place.

words.g: to be necessary (il faut: one must)
words.n: Only in the il form: il faut, one must, it takes. With que it takes the subjonctif.
To come. Venir de + infinitive: to have just done.

words.g: to pass; to spend (time); to stop by

words.n: Of which, whose, about which: replaces de + noun in a clause.
